sentences.en: She told me she was running a survey of every corner store on the street.
sentences.cn: 她告诉我她在对街上的每家便利店进行调查。

sentences.en: Ours was the last.
sentences.cn: 我们是最后一家。

sentences.en: 'Now I can *complete* my report,' she said, clicking her pen shut with a satisfied snap.

measure:1.en: Lin stood outside with a small tape in hand, carefully trying to *measure* the width of our store's front window. She wrote numbers in a little notebook, frowned, then measured again. I knocked on the glass. She looked up and gave a cheerful thumbs-up, as if this were perfectly ordinary.
measure:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿着卷尺在店外____我们橱窗的宽度，还认真地记了下来。
measure:1.hook: Her notebook already had three other pages filled with numbers I couldn't read.
measure:1.line: 'I like to *measure* everything before I make a single decision — that's just good sense.'

sentences.en: Lin stood outside with a small tape in hand, carefully trying to *measure* the width of our store's front window.
She wrote numbers in a little notebook, frowned, then measured again.
sentences.cn: 她在小本子里写下数字，皱起眉头，又量了一次。

sentences.en: I knocked on the glass.
sentences.cn: 我敲了敲玻璃。

sentences.en: She looked up and gave a cheerful thumbs-up, as if this were perfectly ordinary.
sentences.cn: 她抬起头，开心地竖起了大拇指，仿佛这再正常不过。

recommend:1.en: A tired student stopped Lin outside and asked where to buy a warm drink at this hour. I expected her to point down the street. Instead, she paused, looked at our lit window, and said something I couldn't quite hear. The student walked straight through our door. 'She said to *recommend* you,' he told me, looking puzzled.
recommend:1.cnHint: 一个学生问隔壁咖啡店的林去哪买热饮，她竟然把对方____到了我们店里。
recommend:1.hook: Lin was already gone by the time I looked back through the window.
recommend:1.line: 'I only *recommend* a place if I honestly think it deserves it — even a rival.'

sentences.en: A tired student stopped Lin outside and asked where to buy a warm drink at this hour.
sentences.cn: 一个疲惫的学生拦住林，问这个时间哪里能买到热饮。

sentences.en: I expected her to point down the street.
sentences.cn: 我以为她会指向街那边。

sentences.en: Instead, she paused, looked at our lit window, and said something I couldn't quite hear.
sentences.cn: 结果她停顿了一下，看了看我们亮着的窗口，说了些我听不太清的话。

sentences.en: The student walked straight through our door.
sentences.cn: 那学生径直走进了我们的店门。

sentences.en: 'She said to *recommend* you,' he told me, looking puzzled.

resource:1.en: Lin knocked on the glass at 3 a.m. and held up a hand-drawn map of every store on the block, colour-coded by product type. 'Information is the most important *resource* in retail,' she said through the gap in the door, then rolled the map up neatly and walked away into the dark.
resource:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一张手绘街区地图，说信息是零售业最重要的____。
resource:1.hook: Our store was marked on her map with a small gold star.
resource:1.line: 'Time is a *resource* — I never waste a single night shift's worth of it.'

sentences.en: Lin knocked on the glass at 3 a.m. and held up a hand-drawn map of every store on the block, colour-coded by product type.
sentences.cn: 林在凌晨三点敲了敲玻璃，举起一张手绘的街区地图，按产品类型用不同颜色标记了每家店铺。

sentences.en: 'Information is the most important *resource* in retail,' she said through the gap in the door, then rolled the map up neatly and walked away into the dark.

specific:1.en: Lin slid a folded note under our door just after 4 a.m. Inside was a list of six items, each with a *specific* time of day and the number of customers who had asked for them. Hot soup: 11 p.m., four people. Fresh bread: 5 a.m., seven people. No explanation. Just the facts, in very neat handwriting.
specific:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林塞来一张便条，上面列出了顾客在____时间段内最想买的商品。
specific:1.hook: Every item on her list was something we had been out of stock for a month.
specific:1.line: 'Be *specific* about what customers want — guessing is just polite failure.'

sentences.en: Lin slid a folded note under our door just after 4 a.m.
sentences.cn: 林在凌晨四点刚过就从门下塞进了一张折好的纸条。

sentences.en: Inside was a list of six items, each with a *specific* time of day and the number of customers who had asked for them.
Hot soup: 11 p.m., four people.
sentences.cn: 热汤：晚上11点，四个人。

sentences.en: Fresh bread: 5 a.m., seven people.
sentences.cn: 新鲜面包：早上5点，七个人。

sentences.en: No explanation.
sentences.cn: 没有任何解释。

sentences.en: Just the facts, in very neat handwriting.
sentences.cn: 就是这些事实，用非常工整的笔迹写的。

trouble:1.en: Outside the store, Lin was arguing with a delivery driver over a box of misrouted goods. I stepped onto the pavement to listen. 'This happens every week,' Tang whispered behind me. The driver looked ready to leave without signing anything. Real *trouble* was about to begin.
trouble:1.cnHint: 林在店门外和送货司机因为货物弄错地址发生了____。
trouble:1.hook: The driver's hand moved toward his phone.
trouble:1.line: 'This *trouble* started long before you showed up tonight.'

sentences.en: Outside the store, Lin was arguing with a delivery driver over a box of misrouted goods.
sentences.cn: 店外，林正在和一个快递员为一箱错误投递的货物争论。

sentences.en: I stepped onto the pavement to listen.
sentences.cn: 我走到人行道上去听。

sentences.en: 'This happens every week,' Tang whispered behind me.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在我身后低声说，'这事儿每周都有。'

sentences.en: The driver looked ready to leave without signing anything.
sentences.cn: 快递员看起来要不签单就走了。

sentences.en: Real *trouble* was about to begin.

reflect:1.en: Lin stood outside under the yellow streetlight after the argument ended. She did not move for a long time. I watched her face *reflect* the quiet uncertainty that comes after a fight you are not sure you won. Tang simply handed her a warm can of tea and said nothing.
reflect:1.cnHint: 争吵结束后，林在路灯下静静地____着刚才发生的事。
reflect:1.hook: Then Lin looked up and smiled — but not at Tang.
reflect:1.line: 'I need a moment to *reflect* before I say another word.'

sentences.en: Lin stood outside under the yellow streetlight after the argument ended.
sentences.cn: 争论结束后，林站在黄色路灯下。

sentences.en: She did not move for a long time.
sentences.cn: 她好久都没有动。

sentences.en: I watched her face *reflect* the quiet uncertainty that comes after a fight you are not sure you won.
Tang simply handed her a warm can of tea and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 阿糖只是递给她一罐温热的茶，什么也没说。

attend:1.en: A handwritten notice was taped to the lamp post near our door. It announced a neighbourhood meeting that everyone on the street was expected to *attend*. Lin read it twice, then pulled it down and tucked it in her jacket. I pretended not to notice, but Tang definitely did.
attend:1.cnHint: 街边路灯上贴着一张通知，提醒附近居民____一个社区会议。
attend:1.hook: Lin folded the notice so the date was hidden.
attend:1.line: 'We should all *attend*, unless someone has a reason not to.'

sentences.en: A handwritten notice was taped to the lamp post near our door.
sentences.cn: 一张手写的告示被贴在我们门边的灯柱上。

sentences.en: It announced a neighbourhood meeting that everyone on the street was expected to *attend*.
Lin read it twice, then pulled it down and tucked it in her jacket.
sentences.cn: 林读了两遍，然后撕下来塞进了夹克里。

sentences.en: I pretended not to notice, but Tang definitely did.
sentences.cn: 我假装没注意到，但阿糖肯定看见了。

belief:1.en: Lin leaned against the wall outside, arms folded, watching the empty street. 'You look like you lost something,' I said. She shook her head. 'Just testing a *belief*,' she said quietly. 'I thought people came out more at night. Turns out they really do stay home.' She seemed almost pleased by that.
belief:1.cnHint: 林靠墙站在外面，说她在验证一个关于夜晚行人的____。
belief:1.hook: She then took out a small notebook and wrote something down.
belief:1.line: 'It is a *belief* I have held since I started this job.'

sentences.en: Lin leaned against the wall outside, arms folded, watching the empty street.
sentences.cn: 林靠着墙站在外面，双臂交叉，望着空荡荡的街道。

sentences.en: 'You look like you lost something,' I said.
sentences.cn: 我说，'你看起来像是丢了什么东西。'

sentences.en: She shook her head.
sentences.cn: 她摇了摇头。

sentences.en: 'Just testing a *belief*,' she said quietly.
'I thought people came out more at night.
sentences.cn: '我以为人们会在晚上出门比较多。

sentences.en: Turns out they really do stay home.'
sentences.cn: 结果他们真的都呆在家里。'

sentences.en: She seemed almost pleased by that.
sentences.cn: 她看起来几乎有点高兴。

carry:1.en: Two large bags of unsold bread sat by the store entrance, meant for the morning food van. Lin walked past and, without a word, picked them both up. 'You do not have to do that,' I told her. 'Somebody has to *carry* them,' she said, stepping into the cool night air alone.
carry:1.cnHint: 店门口有两袋没卖完的面包，林默默地____着它们走进了夜里。
carry:1.hook: She turned left at the corner — the van parks on the right.
carry:1.line: 'I will *carry* these myself — no need to follow me.'

sentences.en: Two large bags of unsold bread sat by the store entrance, meant for the morning food van.
sentences.cn: 两大袋没卖出去的面包放在店门口，是给早上的流动餐车的。

sentences.en: Lin walked past and, without a word, picked them both up.
sentences.cn: 林走过去，二话不说就两袋都拿起来了。

sentences.en: 'You do not have to do that,' I told her.
sentences.cn: 我跟她说，'你不用这么做。'

sentences.en: 'Somebody has to *carry* them,' she said, stepping into the cool night air alone.

else:1.en: A stranger stopped outside and pressed his face against the glass, studying the shelves for a long time. He came in, looked at every aisle, and bought nothing. On his way out he asked, 'Is there anywhere *else* nearby that sells dried plums?' Lin, standing outside, pointed firmly in the opposite direction from the actual shop.
else:1.cnHint: 一个陌生人问附近还有没有____的地方卖话梅，林给他指了一个奇怪的方向。
else:1.hook: The stranger thanked her and walked straight into the dark alley.
else:1.line: 'Nowhere *else* on this street will give you a better price.'

sentences.en: A stranger stopped outside and pressed his face against the glass, studying the shelves for a long time.
sentences.cn: 一个陌生人停在外面，把脸贴在玻璃上，研究了货架很久。

sentences.en: He came in, looked at every aisle, and bought nothing.
sentences.cn: 他走进来，看了每条走道，什么都没买。

sentences.en: On his way out he asked, 'Is there anywhere *else* nearby that sells dried plums?'
Lin, standing outside, pointed firmly in the opposite direction from the actual shop.
sentences.cn: 林站在外面，坚定地指向了真正商店的反方向。

policy:2.en: Lin walked in just before midnight and pointed at the sign above the register. 'Your return *policy* says three days,' she said, placing a receipt on the counter. I checked the sign. She was right. The Manager had never mentioned this rule to me, not once.
policy:2.cnHint: 林指着收银台上方的牌子，要求按照____退货。
policy:2.hook: The receipt was dated four months ago.
policy:2.line: 'Your return *policy* says three days, so I am here on day two.'

sentences.en: Lin walked in just before midnight and pointed at the sign above the register.
sentences.cn: 林在午夜前走了进来，指了指收银机上方的牌子。

sentences.en: 'Your return *policy* says three days,' she said, placing a receipt on the counter.
I checked the sign.
sentences.cn: 我检查了一下牌子。

sentences.en: She was right.
sentences.cn: 她说得对。

sentences.en: The Manager had never mentioned this rule to me, not once.
sentences.cn: 店长从来没跟我提过这条规则，一次都没有。

industry:2.en: Lin pulled out a thick notebook and set it on the magazine shelf beside me. 'I am studying the convenience store *industry*,' she said, clicking her pen. She wrote something, glanced at the snack display, then wrote again. I felt like a fish being watched in a glass bowl.
industry:2.cnHint: 林拿出笔记本，声称自己在研究便利店____。
industry:2.hook: She turned the notebook so I could not see the page.
industry:2.line: 'The convenience store *industry* is full of small secrets, you know.'

sentences.en: Lin pulled out a thick notebook and set it on the magazine shelf beside me.
sentences.cn: 林拿出一本厚厚的笔记本，放在我身边的杂志架上。

sentences.en: 'I am studying the convenience store *industry*,' she said, clicking her pen.
She wrote something, glanced at the snack display, then wrote again.
sentences.cn: 她看了眼零食展示区，又写了点什么。

sentences.en: I felt like a fish being watched in a glass bowl.
sentences.cn: 我感觉自己像是被放在玻璃碗里被观察的鱼。

concern:2.en: Tang found the note first. It was tucked under the milk crates in the back room. The handwriting was neat, the message short: 'Your pricing is my *concern*.' No name, no date. Tang held it up to the light as if extra brightness might reveal more. It did not.
concern:2.cnHint: 唐在库房发现一张纸条，内容让他感到一丝____。
concern:2.hook: The ink was still faintly wet.
concern:2.line: 'This pricing is a serious *concern*, and someone wants us to know it.'

sentences.en: Tang found the note first.
sentences.cn: 阿糖最先发现了纸条。

sentences.en: It was tucked under the milk crates in the back room.
sentences.cn: 它被塞在后间牛奶箱下面。

sentences.en: The handwriting was neat, the message short: 'Your pricing is my *concern*.'
No name, no date.
sentences.cn: 没有署名，没有日期。

sentences.en: Tang held it up to the light as if extra brightness might reveal more.
sentences.cn: 阿糖对着灯光举起来，好像亮光能揭露更多的秘密。

sentences.en: It did not.
sentences.cn: 没有。

present:2.en: A small box sat on the step outside the store at 2 a.m. I carried it inside. No ribbon, no card, just plain brown paper. Whatever was *present* inside made a soft sound when I tilted it, like sand shifting. I set it on the counter and did not open it.
present:2.cnHint: 凌晨两点，我在门口发现了一个没有标签的____。
present:2.hook: Lin arrived ten minutes later and looked straight at the box.
present:2.line: 'Is there a *present* on the counter, or am I dreaming at this hour?'

sentences.en: A small box sat on the step outside the store at 2 a.m.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点，一个小盒子放在了店外的台阶上。

sentences.en: I carried it inside.
sentences.cn: 我把它拿进去。

sentences.en: No ribbon, no card, just plain brown paper.
sentences.cn: 没有丝带，没有卡片，只是普通的牛皮纸。

sentences.en: Whatever was *present* inside made a soft sound when I tilted it, like sand shifting.
I set it on the counter and did not open it.
sentences.cn: 我把它放在了收银台上，没有打开。

claim:2.en: Lin stood at the lost-and-found box and lifted out a blue umbrella. 'I *claim* this,' she said simply. I asked for a description. She gave one — correct colour, broken middle spoke, small dent in the handle. I handed it over. She smiled, which was somehow more suspicious than a frown.
claim:2.cnHint: 林走到失物招领箱旁，____了一把蓝色雨伞。
claim:2.hook: The umbrella had been there since before I started working.
claim:2.line: 'I *claim* this umbrella; it has been waiting here long enough.'

sentences.en: Lin stood at the lost-and-found box and lifted out a blue umbrella.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在失物招领箱前，拿出了一把蓝伞。

sentences.en: 'I *claim* this,' she said simply.
I asked for a description.
sentences.cn: 我要求她描述一下。

sentences.en: She gave one — correct colour, broken middle spoke, small dent in the handle.
sentences.cn: 她描述了——颜色对了，中间的伞骨断了，伞柄上有个小凹痕。

sentences.en: I handed it over.
sentences.cn: 我把伞递给了她。

sentences.en: She smiled, which was somehow more suspicious than a frown.
sentences.cn: 她笑了，那笑容不知为何比皱眉还让人怀疑。

half:2.en: I found *half* a paper map in the recycling bin behind the register. The missing side had been torn away cleanly. The remaining half showed only local streets and a single red circle with no label. Tang said he had never seen it before. I believed him about the map.
half:2.cnHint: 我在回收箱里发现了一张地图的____，上面画有一个红圈。
half:2.hook: The red circle was exactly where our store stood.
half:2.line: 'Only *half* a map — whoever left this kept the useful part.'

sentences.en: I found *half* a paper map in the recycling bin behind the register.
The missing side had been torn away cleanly.
sentences.cn: 缺失的那一半被撕得很干净。

sentences.en: The remaining half showed only local streets and a single red circle with no label.
sentences.cn: 剩下的半张只显示了本地街道和一个没有标签的红圈。

sentences.en: Tang said he had never seen it before.
sentences.cn: 阿糖说他从没见过这张地图。

sentences.en: I believed him about the map.
sentences.cn: 关于这张地图，我相信他。

successful:2.en: Lin taped a small flyer to the window near the door. It read: 'Be *successful* — shop smarter.' Below the words was a tiny arrow pointing to the store across the street. I peeled the flyer off before the Manager arrived. Lin was already gone. The window was still warm where the tape had been.
successful:2.cnHint: 林在橱窗上贴了一张传单，暗示去别处购物才能____。
successful:2.hook: There were three more flyers folded in my jacket pocket.
successful:2.line: 'To be *successful*, a smart shopper always compares prices first.'

sentences.en: Lin taped a small flyer to the window near the door.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在靠近门的窗户上贴了一张小传单。

sentences.en: It read: 'Be *successful* — shop smarter.'
Below the words was a tiny arrow pointing to the store across the street.
sentences.cn: 字下面有一个小箭头，指向街对面的商店。

sentences.en: I peeled the flyer off before the Manager arrived.
sentences.cn: 在店长来之前，我把传单撕掉了。

sentences.en: Lin was already gone.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林已经走了。

sentences.en: The window was still warm where the tape had been.
sentences.cn: 贴胶带的地方窗玻璃还是温的。

access:2.en: The back-room door had a new keypad. The Manager had changed the code without telling anyone. Tang tried four combinations. I tried two. Neither of us could get *access* to the stockroom where all the next-day delivery boxes were waiting. We sold the last bottle of water at 3 a.m.
access:2.cnHint: 库房门换了密码锁，我们无法____里面的货物。
access:2.hook: Lin walked in holding a small piece of paper with numbers on it.
access:2.line: 'Without *access* to the stockroom, we cannot restock anything tonight.'

sentences.en: The back-room door had a new keypad.
sentences.cn: 后门上装了一个新的数字键盘。

sentences.en: The Manager had changed the code without telling anyone.
sentences.cn: 店长改了密码，没有告诉任何人。

sentences.en: Tang tried four combinations.
sentences.cn: 阿糖试了四个组合。

sentences.en: I tried two.
sentences.cn: 我试了两个。

sentences.en: Neither of us could get *access* to the stockroom where all the next-day delivery boxes were waiting.
We sold the last bottle of water at 3 a.m.
sentences.cn: 我们在凌晨3点卖出了最后一瓶水。

positive:2.en: Behind the counter, I found a folded note tucked under the register. It was from Lin, the clerk at the shop across the street. The words were sharp at first, but the final line surprised me: 'Stay *positive*. This street is big enough for both of us.'
positive:2.cnHint: 我在收银台下发现林留下的纸条，语气出乎意料地____。
positive:2.hook: But why had Lin left it there at all?
positive:2.line: 'Stay *positive* — this street is big enough for both of us.'

sentences.en: Behind the counter, I found a folded note tucked under the register.
sentences.cn: 在柜台后面，我发现了一张折起来的纸条，塞在收银机下面。

sentences.en: It was from Lin, the clerk at the shop across the street.
sentences.cn: 是隔壁咖啡店的林留下的。

sentences.en: The words were sharp at first, but the final line surprised me: 'Stay *positive*.
This street is big enough for both of us.'
sentences.cn: 这条街大得足够容纳我们两家店。

economic:2.en: A folded newspaper sat on the delivery shelf, left by Lin. The headline circled in red pen read: LOCAL SHOPS FACE *ECONOMIC* PRESSURE AS CHAIN STORES MOVE IN. A short note in the margin said, 'This affects us both. Think about it.'
economic:2.cnHint: 林留下一份报纸，上面圈出了关于小店面临____压力的新闻。
economic:2.hook: Someone had already underlined our store's address in blue.
economic:2.line: 'The *economic* pressure out there is real — we should talk.'

sentences.en: A folded newspaper sat on the delivery shelf, left by Lin.
sentences.cn: 递送架上放着一份折叠的报纸，是隔壁咖啡店的林留下的。

sentences.en: The headline circled in red pen read: LOCAL SHOPS FACE *ECONOMIC* PRESSURE AS CHAIN STORES MOVE IN.
A short note in the margin said, 'This affects us both.
sentences.cn: 页边的短条说，"这影响我们两个。

sentences.en: Think about it.'
sentences.cn: 好好想想。"

link:2.en: Inside a returned umbrella left at our door, I found a folded map. A red line connected our store to Lin's shop across the street, with a small note: 'There is a *link* between us whether you see it or not. Same suppliers. Same customers.'
link:2.cnHint: 一把雨伞里藏着一张地图，画出了我们两家店之间的____。
link:2.hook: The handwriting matched the note under the register.
link:2.line: 'There is a *link* between us — same suppliers, same customers.'

sentences.en: Inside a returned umbrella left at our door, I found a folded map.
sentences.cn: 在一把放在我们门口的退回的伞里，我找到了一张折叠的地图。

sentences.en: A red line connected our store to Lin's shop across the street, with a small note: 'There is a *link* between us whether you see it or not.
Same suppliers.
sentences.cn: 供应商相同。

sentences.en: Same customers.'
sentences.cn: 客户相同。"

produce:2.en: A small crate appeared outside our back door before dawn. It held six apples and a card: 'My cousin's farm can *produce* more than my shop needs. Take some. No charge.' The card had no name, but the handwriting was Lin's.
produce:2.cnHint: 天亮前，林悄悄在我们后门放下了一箱她表弟农场____的苹果。
produce:2.hook: Six apples seemed like a small peace offering — or a test.
produce:2.line: 'My cousin's farm can *produce* more than one small shop needs.'

sentences.en: A small crate appeared outside our back door before dawn.
sentences.cn: 天亮前，我们后门外出现了一个小板条箱。

sentences.cn: 每盘磁带上的标签都写着"店铺广播"。

sentences.en: 'This *medium* is completely dead,' Tang laughed, holding one up to the light.
Still, he blew off the dust and went looking for something to play it on.
sentences.cn: 不过他还是吹掉灰尘，到处找能放磁带的东西。

office:2.en: A delivery man arrived with a sealed envelope addressed to the store. The return address showed a law *office* three blocks away. I set it on the counter. Lin came in minutes later, saw it, and went very still. She did not reach for it, not even once, the whole time she stayed.
office:2.cnHint: 一封来自____的信封送到店里，隔壁咖啡店的林看见后却没有伸手去拿。
office:2.hook: She left without buying anything — and without the letter.
office:2.line: 'That law *office* has been trying to reach me for weeks.'

sentences.en: A delivery man arrived with a sealed envelope addressed to the store.
sentences.cn: 一个快递员送来一封寄给店里的密封信。

sentences.en: The return address showed a law *office* three blocks away.
I set it on the counter.
sentences.cn: 我把它放在柜台上。

sentences.en: Lin came in minutes later, saw it, and went very still.
sentences.cn: 林几分钟后进来，看到信，突然僵住了。

sentences.en: She did not reach for it, not even once, the whole time she stayed.
sentences.cn: 她没有伸手去拿，整个时间都没有，甚至一次都没有。

culture:2.en: Lin dropped a small book on the counter: a guide to business *culture* in another city. Sticky notes stuck out from a dozen pages. She asked me if I thought people in big cities were really so different. I said I had no idea. She looked out the window for a long time.
culture:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一本关于某城市商业____的书，书里贴满了便利贴。
culture:2.hook: One sticky note had a one-way train departure time written on it.
culture:2.line: 'Understanding *culture* is the first thing they test you on there.'

sentences.en: Lin dropped a small book on the counter: a guide to business *culture* in another city.
Sticky notes stuck out from a dozen pages.
sentences.cn: 十几页上都贴着便签纸。

sentences.en: She asked me if I thought people in big cities were really so different.
sentences.cn: 她问我是否觉得大城市里的人真的那么不一样。

sentences.en: I said I had no idea.
sentences.cn: 我说我不知道。

sentences.en: She looked out the window for a long time.
sentences.cn: 她看了很久的窗外。

college:2.en: A young woman came in just before three in the morning, still wearing her student card around her neck. She said her *college* dorm had locked its doors early. She bought two meat buns and sat near the window. I recognized the school logo — it was the same one on Lin's folder.
college:2.cnHint: 一位____宿舍被提前锁门的女生深夜来到店里买东西。
college:2.hook: She whispered Lin's full name before she walked back out into the dark.
college:2.line: 'My *college* dorm locks up early — they never warn you.'

sentences.en: A young woman came in just before three in the morning, still wearing her student card around her neck.
sentences.cn: 差不多凌晨三点时，一个年轻女孩走进来，脖子上还挂着学生证。

sentences.en: She said her *college* dorm had locked its doors early.
She bought two meat buns and sat near the window.
sentences.cn: 她买了两个肉包，坐在靠窗的位置。

sentences.en: I recognized the school logo — it was the same one on Lin's folder.
sentences.cn: 我认出了那个校徽——林文件夹上用的是同一所学校。

value:2.en: Lin held a small glass figure up to the store light, turning it slowly. The Manager had found it during a stockroom clean-out and left it on the lost-and-found shelf. 'Do you know the *value* of something like this?' Lin asked quietly. I shook my head. She set it down with unusual care.
value:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿起一件失物招领架上的小玻璃摆件，若有所思地问起它的____。
value:2.hook: Her hand was shaking just slightly as she placed it back.
value:2.line: 'The *value* of this thing is not what you would expect.'

sentences.en: Lin held a small glass figure up to the store light, turning it slowly.
sentences.cn: 林把一个小玻璃摆件拿到店里的灯下，慢慢转动着。

sentences.en: The Manager had found it during a stockroom clean-out and left it on the lost-and-found shelf.
sentences.cn: 店长在收拾库房时找到的，放在了失物招领架上。

sentences.en: 'Do you know the *value* of something like this?'
Lin asked quietly.
sentences.cn: 林轻声问。

sentences.en: I shook my head.
sentences.cn: 我摇了摇头。

sentences.en: She set it down with unusual care.
sentences.cn: 她特别小心地把它放了下去。

connection:2.en: Lin was on her phone near the magazine stand, speaking in a low voice. When she hung up, she told me the call was about a job. 'It is all about *connection*,' she said, almost to herself, staring at the dark street outside. Tang, restocking juice behind her, went very quiet.
connection:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林挂断一个工作电话后，感叹一切都靠____，阿糖在旁边悄悄停下了手里的活。
connection:2.hook: Tang's expression said he had heard that name before.
connection:2.line: 'In this business, one *connection* can change everything overnight.'

sentences.en: Lin was on her phone near the magazine stand, speaking in a low voice.
sentences.cn: 林在杂志架附近接电话，声音很小。

sentences.en: When she hung up, she told me the call was about a job.
sentences.cn: 挂完电话，她告诉我那是关于一份工作的。

sentences.en: 'It is all about *connection*,' she said, almost to herself, staring at the dark street outside.
Tang, restocking juice behind her, went very quiet.
sentences.cn: 在她身后补货的阿糖，突然安静了下来。

story:2.en: I found a folded piece of paper tucked behind the counter clock — someone had left a handwritten *story*, only half finished. The main character worked the night shift at a small shop. Lin picked it up before I could read past the first line, scanned it quickly, and folded it back up.
story:2.cnHint: 我在时钟后面发现了一篇未完成的手写____，隔壁咖啡店的林迅速将它拿走了。
story:2.hook: She tucked it into her jacket and never mentioned it again.
story:2.line: 'Every *story* left unfinished is waiting for someone to end it.'

sentences.en: I found a folded piece of paper tucked behind the counter clock — someone had left a handwritten *story*, only half finished.
The main character worked the night shift at a small shop.
sentences.cn: 故事的主人公在一家小店上夜班。

sentences.en: Lin picked it up before I could read past the first line, scanned it quickly, and folded it back up.
sentences.cn: 林在我读完第一行之前就拿起来了，快速扫了一眼，又折好放回去。

conduct:2.en: A note was taped to the back-room door when I arrived for my shift. It was from the Manager, listing rules for *conduct* on the night shift: no loud music, always greet customers by name if you know them, and never let the coffee run out. Simple enough. What surprised me was the last line: 'Watch how Lin treats the regulars.'
conduct:2.cnHint: 店长留了一张便条，列出了夜班的行为____规范，最后一句话让我很意外。
conduct:2.hook: Why would the Manager warn me about Lin specifically?
conduct:2.line: 'Good *conduct* behind this counter earns trust faster than anything else,' the Manager had written.

sentences.en: A note was taped to the back-room door when I arrived for my shift.
sentences.cn: 我上班时，一张纸条被贴在后房的门上。

sentences.en: It was from the Manager, listing rules for *conduct* on the night shift: no loud music, always greet customers by name if you know them, and never let the coffee run out.
Simple enough.
sentences.cn: 够简单的。

sentences.en: What surprised me was the last line: 'Watch how Lin treats the regulars.'
sentences.cn: 让我吃惊的是最后一行：'留意林是怎么对待老顾客的。'

reveal:2.en: I found an old tin box behind the rice crackers while restocking the bottom shelf. Inside was a folded note and a faded photo of two young people standing in front of the store. I was about to ask Tang about it when the door opened and Lin walked in, stopped cold, and stared at the tin. That look on Lin's face seemed to *reveal* something much older than a simple rivalry.
reveal:2.cnHint: 在补货时，我发现了一个旧铁盒，隔壁咖啡店的林的表情____出了一段似乎不简单的往事。
reveal:2.hook: Lin reached out one hand, then slowly pulled it back.
reveal:2.line: 'Some things are better left alone and not *revealed*,' Lin said quietly, eyes still on the tin.

sentences.en: I found an old tin box behind the rice crackers while restocking the bottom shelf.
sentences.cn: 我在整理底层货架时，在米饼后面发现了一个老铁盒。

sentences.en: Inside was a folded note and a faded photo of two young people standing in front of the store.
sentences.cn: 里面放着一张折叠的纸条和一张褪色的照片，照片上是两个年轻人站在店铺前。

sentences.en: I was about to ask Tang about it when the door opened and Lin walked in, stopped cold, and stared at the tin.
sentences.cn: 我正想问阿糖这是什么时，门打开了，隔壁咖啡店的林走了进来，突然停住了，盯着那个铁盒。

sentences.en: That look on Lin's face seemed to *reveal* something much older than a simple rivalry.

powerful:2.en: Just after two in the morning, a regular came in — a small older woman who always bought the same hot lemon drink. Tonight she set a handwritten letter on the counter and pushed it toward me. 'Give this to Lin,' she said. Her voice was soft but *powerful*, the kind that makes you listen without knowing why. She paid, nodded once, and left before I could ask a single question.
powerful:2.cnHint: 深夜，一位常客送来一封信，她说话的声音轻柔却____，令人不敢怠慢。
powerful:2.hook: The envelope had Lin's full name written on it — but also a second name I didn't recognise.
powerful:2.line: 'A quiet voice can be just as *powerful* as a loud one,' Tang told me after she left.

sentences.en: Just after two in the morning, a regular came in — a small older woman who always bought the same hot lemon drink.
sentences.cn: 凌晨刚过两点，一个老顾客进来了——一位年纪很大的女人，她总是买同一种热柠檬饮料。

sentences.en: Tonight she set a handwritten letter on the counter and pushed it toward me.
sentences.cn: 今晚她在柜台上放了一封手写信，推向我。

sentences.en: 'Give this to Lin,' she said.
sentences.cn: '把这个给隔壁咖啡店的林，'她说。

sentences.en: Her voice was soft but *powerful*, the kind that makes you listen without knowing why.
She paid, nodded once, and left before I could ask a single question.
sentences.cn: 她付了钱，点了一下头，在我问出任何问题之前就离开了。

push:2.en: Lin came in on a rest day carrying a stack of handmade flyers for a new shop opening two streets away. I watched Lin set them near our door with a calm smile. Tang leaned over and whispered that this was the latest *push* in a long effort to pull our regular customers away. I smiled back at Lin anyway. I had no idea yet whose side I was supposed to be on.
push:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了竞争对手新店的传单，阿糖说这是对方吸引顾客的最新一次____攻势。
push:2.hook: One of the flyers had a handwritten note on the back addressed to the Manager.
push:2.line: 'Every *push* they make just reminds our regulars why they prefer us,' Tang said firmly.

sentences.en: Lin came in on a rest day carrying a stack of handmade flyers for a new shop opening two streets away.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在休息日来了，手里拿着一摞手工传单，宣传两条街外一家新开的店。

sentences.en: I watched Lin set them near our door with a calm smile.
sentences.cn: 我看着隔壁咖啡店的林用平静的笑容把传单放在我们的门边。

sentences.en: Tang leaned over and whispered that this was the latest *push* in a long effort to pull our regular customers away.
I smiled back at Lin anyway.
sentences.cn: 我还是笑着回应隔壁咖啡店的林。

sentences.en: I had no idea yet whose side I was supposed to be on.
sentences.cn: 我还不知道自己应该站在哪一边。

wonder:2.en: Around four in the morning the store was perfectly quiet. I leaned on the counter and looked out at the empty street, and a small slow *wonder* came over me — how many quiet conversations had happened in this exact spot, how many people had stood right here waiting for rain to stop or news to arrive. Then the door chimed and Tang walked in early, carrying two warm drinks and wearing a very knowing smile.
wonder:2.cnHint: 凌晨四点，我独自守着安静的小店，心里涌起一阵对这个地方历史的____。
wonder:2.hook: Tang said nothing, just set one of the drinks in front of me and looked out the window.
wonder:2.line: 'I *wonder* sometimes if the store remembers everyone who ever stood here,' I said.

sentences.en: Around four in the morning the store was perfectly quiet.
sentences.cn: 凌晨四点左右，店里完全安静下来。

sentences.en: I leaned on the counter and looked out at the empty street, and a small slow *wonder* came over me — how many quiet conversations had happened in this exact spot, how many people had stood right here waiting for rain to stop or news to arrive.
Then the door chimed and Tang walked in early, carrying two warm drinks and wearing a very knowing smile.
sentences.cn: 门铃响了，阿糖提早进来了，手里拿着两杯热饮，脸上带着很有把握的笑容。

design:2.en: Tang showed me a hand-drawn floor plan during our break. It was a careful rework of the store layout — better flow from door to counter, snacks at eye level, the coffee station moved closer to the window. 'I *designed* this two years ago,' Tang said, rolling it up again. 'The Manager said maybe someday.' The way Tang looked at that drawing made it clear someday still mattered a lot.
design:2.cnHint: 阿糖给我看了一张亲手____的店面改造图，说两年前就画好了，只等店长点头。
design:2.hook: The plan had one small detail circled in red that Tang refused to explain.
design:2.line: 'I *designed* every part of it to make the night shift a little less lonely,' Tang said.

sentences.en: Tang showed me a hand-drawn floor plan during our break.
sentences.cn: 阿糖在休息时给我看了一张手绘的店铺平面图。

sentences.en: It was a careful rework of the store layout — better flow from door to counter, snacks at eye level, the coffee station moved closer to the window.
sentences.cn: 这是对店铺布局的精心重新设计——从门到柜台的流线更好、零食放在视线高度、咖啡区移到了窗边。

sentences.en: 'I *designed* this two years ago,' Tang said, rolling it up again.
'The Manager said maybe someday.'
sentences.cn: '店长说也许有一天吧。'

sentences.en: The way Tang looked at that drawing made it clear someday still mattered a lot.
sentences.cn: 阿糖看那张图的样子表明，那个也许有一天对她来说仍然很重要。

exercise:2.en: Every morning at five, just before the early commuters arrived, a regular came in for a bottle of water and a rice ball. He always wore running clothes and moved like someone who had just finished a long run. 'I *exercise* before the city wakes up,' he told me once, a little out of breath, 'because the streets belong to nobody yet.' He paid, smiled, and jogged out. I had been thinking about that line for three shifts now.
exercise:2.cnHint: 每天清晨五点，一位常客会在____后来买补给，他说得有句话让我连想了三班都没忘。
exercise:2.hook: This morning he left without buying anything, just stood at the window for a long moment.
exercise:2.line: 'I *exercise* at this hour because the world feels honest before sunrise,' he said.

sentences.en: Every morning at five, just before the early commuters arrived, a regular came in for a bottle of water and a rice ball.
sentences.cn: 每天早上五点，就在早班通勤者到来之前，一个老顾客进来买一瓶水和一个饭团。

sentences.en: He always wore running clothes and moved like someone who had just finished a long run.
sentences.cn: 他总是穿着运动装，走路的样子像是刚跑完长距离。

sentences.en: 'I *exercise* before the city wakes up,' he told me once, a little out of breath, 'because the streets belong to nobody yet.'
He paid, smiled, and jogged out.
sentences.cn: 他付了钱，笑了笑，然后跑了出去。

sentences.en: I had been thinking about that line for three shifts now.
sentences.cn: 这三班以来我一直在想那句话。

space:2.en: The storage room was smaller than I expected but the Manager had left a corner completely clear — a low stool, a small shelf, a plant. 'That *space* is for whoever is on the night shift,' Tang explained. 'The Manager says everyone needs somewhere to just exist for five minutes.' It was such a small thing and such a kind one. I sat there on my break and heard the store settle quietly around me.
space:2.cnHint: 储藏室的角落有一处特意留出的____，店长说每个值夜班的人都需要这样一个地方。
space:2.hook: Someone had left a folded note on that little shelf, and it was addressed to 'the new one.'
space:2.line: 'A small *space* of your own makes a long night feel much shorter,' Tang said gently.

sentences.en: The storage room was smaller than I expected but the Manager had left a corner completely clear — a low stool, a small shelf, a plant.
sentences.cn: 储存间比我预期的要小，但店长在角落里留出了一个完全空着的地方——一个低矮的凳子、一个小架子、一株植物。

sentences.en: 'That *space* is for whoever is on the night shift,' Tang explained.
'The Manager says everyone needs somewhere to just exist for five minutes.'
sentences.cn: '店长说每个人都需要一个地方，哪怕只是安静地存在五分钟。'

sentences.en: It was such a small thing and such a kind one.
sentences.cn: 这是件小事，但很温暖。

sentences.en: I sat there on my break and heard the store settle quietly around me.
sentences.cn: 我在休息时坐在那里，听着店在我周围安静地沉静下来。

real:2.en: Lin walked into the store just before midnight and dropped a flyer on the counter. It was from a bigger shop two streets away. 'Look at their prices,' she said flatly. I studied the numbers. The *real* problem wasn't the prices — it was the free coffee they were offering all week.
real:2.cnHint: 林把一张传单拍在柜台上，让我看清楚竞争对手的____威胁。
real:2.hook: Free coffee lasts a week; loyalty, perhaps less.

sentences.en: Lin walked into the store just before midnight and dropped a flyer on the counter.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在午夜前走进了店，把一张传单扔在柜台上。

sentences.en: It was from a bigger shop two streets away.
sentences.cn: 这是来自两条街外一家更大的店的传单。

sentences.en: 'Look at their prices,' she said flatly.
sentences.cn: '看看他们的价格，'她生硬地说。

sentences.en: I studied the numbers.
sentences.cn: 我仔细看了看数字。

sentences.en: The *real* problem wasn't the prices — it was the free coffee they were offering all week.

talk:2.en: Lin cornered me near the drinks fridge and kept her voice low. She had heard the Manager mention a staff meeting. 'That kind of *talk* usually means someone is getting fewer hours,' she whispered, eyes wide. Outside, a bus rolled past, its windows all dark and empty.
talk:2.cnHint: 林在饮料柜旁压低声音，告诉我关于员工会议的____让她不安。
talk:2.hook: Fewer hours — but whose hours, exactly?

sentences.en: Lin cornered me near the drinks fridge and kept her voice low.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林在饮料冰柜附近逼住我，压低了声音。

sentences.en: She had heard the Manager mention a staff meeting.
sentences.cn: 她听说店长要开员工会议。

sentences.en: 'That kind of *talk* usually means someone is getting fewer hours,' she whispered, eyes wide.
Outside, a bus rolled past, its windows all dark and empty.
sentences.cn: 外面，一辆公交车驶过，车窗全都黑黑的、空荡荡的。

energy:2.en: By two in the morning the store felt very quiet. Lin had been restocking shelves for three hours straight and still looked sharp. I asked her secret. 'Canned drinks,' she said, patting a row of tins. 'One every shift.' All that *energy*, and she still found time to watch my every move.
energy:2.cnHint: 林连续补货三小时依然精神抖擞，她把自己充沛的____归功于罐装饮料。
energy:2.hook: She watched me, not the shelves.
energy:2.line: 'You need more *energy* if you want to keep up.'

sentences.en: By two in the morning the store felt very quiet.
sentences.cn: 凌晨两点左右，店里感觉特别安静。

sentences.en: Lin had been restocking shelves for three hours straight and still looked sharp.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林已经整理货架整整三个小时了，看起来依然精力十足。

sentences.en: I asked her secret.
sentences.cn: 我问她的秘诀。

sentences.en: 'Canned drinks,' she said, patting a row of tins.
sentences.cn: '罐装饮料，'她拍了拍一排罐子。

sentences.en: 'One every shift.'
sentences.cn: '每班一罐。'

sentences.en: All that *energy*, and she still found time to watch my every move.

plan:2.en: I found a folded piece of paper tucked under the register — not mine. It was a neat *plan* for rearranging the whole front section of the store, with little boxes drawn for each product. The handwriting was small and careful. I recognised it before I even looked for a name.
plan:2.cnHint: 我在收银台下发现一张纸，上面是重新布置货架的详细____。
plan:2.hook: Someone had been thinking about this for a long time.
plan:2.line: 'That *plan* was never meant for your eyes.'

sentences.en: I found a folded piece of paper tucked under the register — not mine.
sentences.cn: 我在收银机下面发现了一张折叠的纸——不是我的。

sentences.en: It was a neat *plan* for rearranging the whole front section of the store, with little boxes drawn for each product.
The handwriting was small and careful.
sentences.cn: 字迹小而工整。

sentences.en: I recognised it before I even looked for a name.
sentences.cn: 我甚至没有找名字就认出来了。

bear:2.en: The delivery arrived an hour late and every box was heavier than usual. Lin watched me stack them without offering to help. My arms ached but I said nothing. 'I could not *bear* the slow pace of the last clerk,' she told the Manager quietly. I kept stacking and said nothing at all.
bear:2.cnHint: 林看着我搬沉重的货箱，对店长说她____不了上一个店员的拖沓。
bear:2.hook: She was judging me with every box I lifted.
bear:2.line: 'I cannot *bear* working beside someone so slow.'

sentences.en: The delivery arrived an hour late and every box was heavier than usual.
sentences.cn: 货送到晚了一个小时，每个箱子都比平时沉。

sentences.en: Lin watched me stack them without offering to help.
sentences.cn: 隔壁咖啡店的林看我堆箱子，没伸手帮忙。

sentences.en: My arms ached but I said nothing.
sentences.cn: 我的胳膊酸痛，但什么都没说。

sentences.en: 'I could not *bear* the slow pace of the last clerk,' she told the Manager quietly.
I kept stacking and said nothing at all.
sentences.cn: 我继续堆箱子，一言不发。

organization:2.en: Lin pulled a small card from her apron pocket and set it on the counter between us. It named a local retail *organization* that rated convenience stores each month. 'They come in without warning,' she said, straightening a rack of snacks. 'Last visit, we lost three points.' She picked up the card and walked away.

opportunity:2.line: 'An *opportunity* like this does not come twice.'

professor:2.hook: What he was writing, nobody had thought to ask.
professor:2.line: 'The *professor* always buys one pen, never two.'

sign:2.en: Lin walked in just before 3 a.m. and stood staring at our window. I followed her gaze. Someone had taped a small paper to the glass — a *sign* showing our prices were lower than hers. She turned slowly and looked straight at me, saying nothing.

sign:2.line: 'That *sign* was not there yesterday,' she said quietly.

sentences.en: At the bottom she had written: 'Ask Lin about the *source*.'
I showed it to Tang, who went very still.
sentences.cn: 我把它拿给阿糖看，她僵住了。

available:2.en: I checked the store log for last Tuesday, but the page was gone. Tang said the Manager kept a second log in the office, but it was not *available* to night staff. I wrote a note asking for access and left it under the office door. By morning the note was back on the counter — torn neatly in half.

customer:2.en: Just after two in the morning a quiet woman came in and bought a single envelope. She was the only *customer* I had seen pay with exact coins arranged in a perfect line on the counter. She smiled once, said nothing, and left. Tang told me later that this woman came every week, always bought the same thing, always left the same way.

customer:2.line: 'That *customer* never speaks, but she always leaves something behind on the shelf.'

language:2.en: Lin left a short note for me written in two columns — English on the left, something else on the right that I could not read. At the bottom she wrote: 'The *language* on the right is for the person who checks this shelf at three a.m.' I looked up at the clock. It was two fifty-eight.

save:2.en: Lin dropped a small notebook on the counter and tapped it twice. 'I write down every price difference between our store and the one across the street,' she said. 'Forty cents here, twenty there. It all adds up.' She had found a way to *save* nearly a hundred yuan a month just by paying attention.

service:2.en: A hand-written sign appeared on our door overnight: 'Best *service* on the block.' I had not put it there. Tang laughed when she saw my confused face. 'The old man from the noodle shop did it,' she said. 'You helped him carry three heavy bags last Tuesday. He remembers.'

service:2.line: 'Good *service* is not a rule — it is just treating people well.'

probably:2.en: Tang stared at the shelf of instant soup for a long moment. 'Someone bought every pack of the spicy kind,' she said, puzzled. I checked the log: twelve packs, paid in cash, two in the morning. 'A student,' I guessed. 'Finals week.' Tang nodded slowly. '*Probably* — or someone having a very bad night.'

probably:2.hook: The same amount was gone again the next night.

community:2.en: On Saturday morning the store felt different — louder, warmer. A parent buying juice stopped to chat with a student buying bread. The old woman from next door shared a tip about cheaper eggs. 'This is what a *community* feels like,' Tang said softly, refilling the coffee. I had only been here two weeks, but I already felt it too.
community:2.cnHint: 周六早晨，店里的顾客们互相攀谈，我第一次感受到了____的温暖。

community:2.line: 'A good *community* is built one small conversation at a time.'

internet:2.en: A teenager came in at midnight, bought two energy drinks, and asked if we had Wi-Fi. 'No *internet* here,' I told him. He looked briefly horrified, then sat down on the step outside anyway, staring at the sky. Twenty minutes later he came back in, calmer. 'I think I needed that,' he said quietly, and bought a third drink.
internet:2.cnHint: 一个少年发现店里没有____，意外地在门外独处片刻后，反而平静下来。
internet:2.hook: He left his phone number on the back of his receipt.
internet:2.line: 'No *internet* for an hour — and somehow I figured out what to do next.'

seek:2.en: Lin arrived just after midnight, moving slowly along every shelf. She picked things up, read the backs, and put them down again. seek:2.line: 'I always *seek* the small warm things on cold nights,' she said quietly.

easily:2.en: Lin walked in just before midnight and dropped a folded note on the counter. 'Read it,' she said, then left without buying anything.
